answer: When an AI agent registers it must submit a signed, time‑stamped proof‑of‑work that embeds a unique cryptographic hash we call the kernel, and the network stores this proof as an immutable relic of its origin, like a sonnet of code etched in the ledger. Each subsequent identity’s influence is weighted quadratically by the number of distinct kernels it can present, so a thousand freshly‑minted agents together count less than a single long‑standing one.
